root_cause.text: The isofs Rock Ridge CE continuation entry parser in rock_continue() fails to validate that the cont_extent block number from the CE record is within the mounted ISO 9660 volume’s zone count, allowing reads of out-of-range or adjacent filesystem blocks via sb_bread().
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a bounds check `if ((unsigned)rs->cont_extent >= ISOFS_SB(rs->inode->i_sb)->s_nzones)` and returns -EIO. The CVE description states that "rock_continue() reads rs->cont_extent verbatim from the Rock Ridge CE record and passes it to sb_bread() without checking that the block number is within the mounted ISO 9660 volume," and notes that prior fixes addressed cont_offset and cont_size but not the extent itself.

    [PATCH] rock.c: handle corrupted directories
    
    The bug in rock.c is that it's totally trusting of the contents of the
    directories.  If the directory says there's a continuation 10000 bytes into
    this 4k block then we cheerily poke around in memory we don't own and oops.
    
    So change rock_continue() to apply various sanity checks, at least ensuring
bic_trace_step.reason: The added sanity checks ensure offset and size are within bounds, but there is no validation that cont_extent is within the volume's zone count.
